classification.difficultyReason: Combine power parity, reflection and horizontal and vertical shifts to select the sketch with the correct orientation and turning or inflection location.

content.prompt: Which of the following could be the graph of each function?

spec.description: Four separate, unticked coordinate systems in one horizontal comparison row. All curves increase. A has its flat region near the y-axis below the x-axis; B right and above; C left and above; D left and below. Numerical drawing coordinates are schematic and are not student givens.
spec.mathematics: Increasing cubic profiles with distinct horizontal and vertical placements of their inflection points; arrowheads on both axes and both curve ends.
spec.answerVisibility: All four options are permanent student-visible givens; no correct option is marked.

answer.worked: Translate $y=x^3$ three units left and two units down. The increasing curve has its inflection point at $(-3,-2)$, left of the $y$-axis and below the $x$-axis. Correct answer: D.

spec.description: Four increasing cubic options in a horizontal row. A flattens right and above, with negative y-intercept; B left and above, with positive y-intercept; C right and below, with negative y-intercept; D near the y-axis below the x-axis. No numerical ticks or coordinates are printed.
spec.mathematics: Schematic translated cubic profiles preserve the source inflection-point quadrants and intercept relationships.
spec.answerVisibility: All options remain visible; the supplied answer belongs only in answer fields.

answer.worked: Translate $y=x^3$ three units left and four units up. The increasing curve has its inflection point at $(-3,4)$, left of the $y$-axis and above the $x$-axis. Correct answer: B.

spec.description: Four flat-bottomed or flat-topped quartic profiles touching the x-axis. A opens down on the left; B opens up on the left; C opens down on the right; D opens up on the right. Separate unticked arrowed axes and curve-end arrows are retained.
spec.mathematics: Even fourth-power curves have horizontal tangency at their turning points. A and C have maxima; B and D have minima. Unlabelled schematic coordinates are used only to reproduce these relationships.
spec.answerVisibility: All four supplied options are visible without answer markings.

answer.worked: Reflect $y=x^4$ in the $x$-axis and translate it three units right. The curve opens downward and has its turning point at $(3,0)$. Correct answer: C.

spec.description: Four increasing fifth-power profiles with pronounced flat central regions. A is right and above; B left and above; C right and below; D left and below. Axis and curve arrows, x/y labels and the horizontal option order are retained; no numerical scale is asserted.
spec.mathematics: Odd fifth-power profiles have inflection points rather than turning points. Their source quadrants and visible intercept relationships distinguish the options.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent comparison options only; no answer or derived coordinate labels are printed.

answer.worked: Translate $y=x^5$ three units left and two units down. The increasing curve has its inflection point at $(-3,-2)$, left of the $y$-axis and below the $x$-axis. Correct answer: D.

spec.description: Four decreasing cubic options. A flattens left and above; B right and above; C left and below; D right and below. Preserve the visible intercept relationships, unticked axes, labels and end arrows. Drawing coordinates are schematic rather than supplied numerical values.
spec.mathematics: Reflected cubic profiles with their inflection points in the four source quadrants.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied options are student-visible; the correct option is unmarked.

answer.worked: Reflect $y=x^3$ in the $x$-axis, then translate it two units left and one unit up. The decreasing curve has its inflection point at $(-2,1)$, left of the $y$-axis and above the $x$-axis. Correct answer: A.
